messages:
ada: Heads-up — I hit a production error pattern: some customer traffic routed to v1 pools even though their SDK sends v2 semantics. 401s and unexpected quota checks.
chris: Can you paste an example request? Is this the header-based routing issue we talked about in the doc?
ada: Example: client sends `X-Redwood-Version: 2` (no `v`), but our router only matches `v2` and fallback logic treats it as unknown -> route->v1 fallback path that expects legacy auth format.
sasha: Ah, casing/format normalization bug again? Do we canonicalize header values anywhere?
ada: We normalize header keys but not values. Also the routing precedence code does: explicit route rule -> path prefix -> header exact-match -> token prefix. We accidentally have a strict equality check for "v2" (string) which rejects "2" and "2.0".
chris: That explains it. Impact: customers using newer SDK releases (that send numeric version) get misrouted. How many hits?
ada: ~0.6% of traffic in the last 24h for one high-volume tenant, all from a handful of SDK builds. Telemetry shows increased auth failures and then fallback to dedicated v1 pools.
pm-annie: This has product impact — billing and SLAs could be off. What's a quick mitigation?
ada: Propose a compatibility shim that expands accepted values and records an `inferred_version` telemetry tag. Also add a short-lived tolerant-match path that accepts numeric forms. Example mapping rule:```
# routing precedence (new)
1) route.rule.version_header (explicit)
2) route.rule.path_prefix
3) header match normalized: lower(headerValue) in {"v2","2","2.0"}
4) token prefix inference
5) fallback: v1
```
chris: Additive change is low-risk. But quota semantics: if we route to v2 for some requests while billing is still v1, customers might be double-counted or hit wrong quota buckets.
ada: Right — plan: when tolerant match is used, mark the request with `compat_window` tag for 1h where quota attribution increments both v1 and v2 counters (no double-billing to the customer; internal attribution only) and the console shows a merged view. After the window, we commit to single-bucket attribution.
sasha: We should avoid changing private deployments silently. Feature-flag it per-deployment. Also add an opt-out header `X-Redwood-Compat: off`.
ops: From infra side, we need metrics: `routing_reason`, `header_value_raw`, `normalized_header`, `matched_version`, `compat_shim_applied`. Please add those to the telemetry event schema so we can alert on upticks.
ada: Will include. Also propose a small e2e test in the router repo that sends permutations: `v2`, `2`, `2.0`, `V2`, `v-2` and asserts matching logic and quota tagging.
chris: What's rollout plan and mitigation if something breaks?
ada: Canary at 1% for 6 hours (traffic steering by sdk-agent header), monitor auth failures, quota mismatches, and `compat_shim_applied` rate. If green, ramp to 25% then 100% over two days. Rollback if auth failures + increased 5xx > 0.5%.
pm-annie: Console UX: we need a per-tenant deprecation banner that says "We detected ambiguous version headers — we applied compatibility mode. Please update SDKs." Also surface counts of affected requests and earliest SDK versions.
sasha: I'll add a small dashboard tile: timeseries of `compat_shim_applied` and top `header_value_raw` by tenant.
ada: PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/router/pulls/459 (adds tolerant-match + telemetry + feature flag). Deploy-bot: can you queue a canary when PR merges? :rocket:
deploy-bot: Canary job queued for canary-1 (1% traffic) once PR merges. Link: https://ci.internal/rw/459/canary
ops: One more: ensure private/private-onprem customers get opt-in only. We must add a migration note to the private-deploy README and send a heads-up to account execs for impacted tenants.
pm-annie: I'll draft the customer message (short + SDK bump instructions).
chris: Thanks everyone — looks like low-risk fix, docs + telemetry covered. Please paste the test matrix in the PR and I'll approve after green CI. :+1:
